newsitem.title: BELGIUM: European buyers replace tallow with palm products.
newsitem.headline: European buyers replace tallow with palm products.

text.p: Buyers of tallow in the European oleochemicals industry are increasingly asking to replace the animal fat with oil palm products, said Claire Lange of Unichema International, the chemicals arm of Unilever NV..

"...in recent times the whole industry has seen with increasing momentum a shift from tallow to the vegetable substitute -- palm oil," Lange, a marketing manager at Unichema in the Netherlands, told the Lipidex 97 oilseeds conference..

"What the future will bring...is predominantly dependent upon a combination of the economics of tallow versus palm oil as well as Health and Safety Legislation related to Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE, or mad cow disease).
Tallow has been declared safe if effective rendering processes are in place.
But it is being associated with risks to human health from beef consumption after new evidence that BSE may be linked to a human equivalent.
Vegetable products also appealed to those consumers perceiving them emotionally as healthier and environmentally friendly, Lange said.
Raw materials buyers were also closely watching the tallow-palm oil price relationship.
Lange said renderers, who process animal remains, and oleochemical producers needed a continuous dialogue assessing the needs of the market in order to safeguard tallow sales.
She said it was hard to quantify the size of the shifts at the moment as many feedstock products could substitute each other and buying depended on price, availability and customer specifications.
Tallow accounts for roughly a third of oleochemical feedstock in Europe.
Delegates said the EU produces one million tonnes of tallow a year and imports 500,000 tonnes, of which 350,000 tonnes come from the United States.
The oleochemical industry produces fatty acids, glycerine and various derivatives for soap, chemicals and feed uses.
Apart from tallow and palm oil, they also buy palm kernel and coconut oil and derivates of all the products.
